method: IRONMAN's official performance-based qualification as revised in November 2025, implemented from public data. Each age-group winner earns an automatic World Championship slot; the remaining performance slots are split into a men's and a women's pool sized by each gender's share of age-group starters, and each pool goes to the athletes whose age-graded time (finish ÷ their age-group Kona Standard) ranks highest within that gender. The Kona Standard is the average of the fastest 20% of World Championship finish times over the last 5 editions (Kona and Nice), per age group per gender. Each race uses a fixed slot allocation (~40, larger for a few big races). Qualifying time = the slowest finish time that still earned a slot. Independent historical estimate — not a guarantee. Figures are the median of the last editions with a min–max range.

rollDown.note: Roll-down scenarios (rollMedianFmt / rollFmt), keyed by the assumed percentage of offered slots that get accepted. Declined slots roll down within the same gender's pool, so the real cutoff is slower than the pure allocation. These rates are ASSUMPTIONS, not measurements: IRONMAN publishes no per-age-group acceptance data — only that 15% of women's and 3% of men's automatic slots rolled on. Present them as scenarios and state the rate alongside the time.
